name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,423

clue.text: Drive away from party around half nine

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word means only its first two letters are kept
the party word is wrapped around the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: a bash is an informal word for a party
the front half of the number word

explanation.surface: Someone is ejected from a celebration at about half past nine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half nine' looks like a time of day; here it means half the word, its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To banish someone is to expel or send them off, forcing them out of a place.

clue.text: Working on Bruce's delivery

indicators.note: something working is in operation or being worked over, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the fodder letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone called Bruce is practising his bowling or his speech delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bouncer is a short-pitched ball that rears up at the batsman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer is one particular kind of ball bowled in cricket, so it is an example of a delivery.

clue.text: Gentle reminder from Georgia after horse gets upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the horse word is read bottom to top
the country piece is placed after the horse piece in the answer

blocks.note: a dun is a greyish-brown horse
GE is the international code for the country Georgia

explanation.surface: A reminder comes from someone in Georgia after a horse becomes distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia here is the country, not the US state, so its two-letter international code is used; in a down clue 'upset' turns the horse upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a light prod, and figuratively a soft prompt to remember or act on something.

clue.text: Astonishing events almost certain to have rebels coming under pressure

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
in a down clue, coming under places the rebels word beneath the pressure abbreviation

blocks.note: sure is a synonym of certain
P is the physics symbol for pressure
rises as a verb: rebels, rises up

explanation.surface: Shocking events seem nearly inevitable when rebels are put under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: SUR(e), then P, then RISES below it.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprises are unexpected happenings that astonish people, plural like the clue's events.

clue.text: Handy to keep foreign article on computer programming language becoming obsolete

indicators.note: on places the article directly before the language letter in an across answer
the handy word keeps, holding inside itself, the other pieces

blocks.note: deft means skilful, handy
un is the French indefinite article
C is a well-known programming language

explanation.surface: A useful foreign piece on coding is going out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: DEF(UN C)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something defunct no longer exists or functions, which is what out of use and outmoded means.

clue.text: Went back to find plant embedded firmly

indicators.note: going back means the word for went is read from end to start

blocks.note: went, colloquially, as in relieved oneself
to set is to plant, as in setting seeds

explanation.surface: A gardener returned to see a plant well rooted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went back' looks like plain movement; it is a slangy went (urinated) reversed. PEED backwards gives DEEP, then SET.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-set describes something firmly fixed far in, like deep-set eyes or a deep-set belief.

clue.text: Fellow novelist's worthless ideas

blocks.note: F is a standard abbreviation for fellow
Philip Roth, the American novelist

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a writer's empty notions.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth is empty, insubstantial talk or thought with no real substance, like foam on a drink.

clue.text: Sarkozy's denial about being in trouble after opening of proceedings is without equal

indicators.note: the opening of a word is just its first letter
being in puts the short word for about inside the trouble word
after places the trouble piece later in the answer than the opening letter

blocks.note: a Frenchman such as Sarkozy says non for no
first letter of proceedings
to ail is to trouble or afflict
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A French president's refusal to be troubled at the start of a case is unmatched.
explanation.walkthrough: NON + P + A(RE)IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil, from French for no equal, describes someone or something unrivalled and peerless.

clue.text: The aim of Flirtbox members until now

definitions.note: cryptic: the purpose of joining a dating site is to go on a date

blocks.note: Flirtbox is a dating website, so its users want to go out with someone
second meaning: up to the present moment

explanation.surface: What people on a dating site are hoping for, so far.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as an infinitive, the answer is what dating-site members want; read as a phrase, it means so far.
explanation.definitionFit: To date is an everyday adverbial phrase meaning up to the present time, so far.

clue.text: Occupy one's spare time making punch

blocks.note: first meaning: to fill gaps in a schedule
second meaning: British slang for giving someone a beating

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a hobby of making a fruity drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like the drink; it is the British slang sense, to beat someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: To fill in idle hours is to pass them, and in British slang to fill someone in is to thrash them.

clue.text: Stress caused by row with subordinate

blocks.note: under means lower in rank
a row of things is a line

explanation.surface: Workplace tension arising from an argument with a junior employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel; it is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise it, just as a stroke beneath words gives them emphasis.

clue.text: Days after, wife is snatched by one possessed

indicators.note: the wife letter is seized and held inside the number word
the days abbreviation is placed after the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
W is a standard abbreviation for wife
D abbreviates days

explanation.surface: Later, a wife is abducted by a demon-possessed figure.
explanation.walkthrough: O(W)NE + D.
explanation.definitionFit: Owned is a past form meaning had as one's property, the same sense as possessed.

clue.text: Disappear completely

blocks.note: first meaning: as in ... off or the fog ...
second meaning: an adverb

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one instruction, vanish entirely; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Mist or a crowd clears when it vanishes, and clear as adverb means entirely, as in clear through.

clue.text: Become despondent as Bethany would if husband left

definitions.text: as Bethany would if husband left
definitions.note: cryptic: the name's middle letter is H

blocks.note: first meaning: to lose courage or hope

blocks.clueFragment: as Bethany would if husband left
blocks.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter name is H, the abbreviation for husband, so removing it takes out its centre

explanation.surface: A woman named Bethany would be crushed if her husband walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a sad marriage; the second reading is literal: drop H from the middle of the name and it loses its central letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose heart is an idiom for becoming discouraged and giving up hope.

clue.text: Enlists most of the others without work at home

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter
without here means outside, so the others word goes around the work piece

blocks.note: the rest means the others
op is short for opus, a work
in means at home

explanation.surface: Signs up most of the unemployed people staying at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without work' looks like jobless; 'without' is the old sense, outside, so the shortened others word goes around the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope someone in is to persuade or recruit them to join an activity.

clue.text: Submit posts revealing prearranged conspiracies

blocks.note: to put up a candidate or proposal is to submit it
posts are positions of employment

explanation.surface: Filing job applications exposes rigged appointments.
explanation.definitionFit: A put-up job is a scheme secretly arranged in advance to deceive, such as a fake robbery.

clue.text: Kind offer

blocks.note: first meaning: gentle, caring
second meaning: a formal bid, as for a contract

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a generous proposal; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means soft-hearted and caring, and as a noun a tender is a formal bid to supply goods.

clue.text: Inattentive when seconds away from breaking linnet's egg

indicators.note: the seconds letter goes away, removed from the bird phrase
breaking an egg smashes it, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for seconds
the letters as written, including the possessive S

explanation.surface: Someone careless cracks a small songbird's egg in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: A linnet is a small finch. Remove the S from LINNETSEGG, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Negligent describes failing to take proper care or pay attention, a synonym of heedless.

clue.text: Piece of inexpensive padding surprisingly stops condition affecting eyelid

indicators.note: a piece of a word here is just its first letter
padding fills out the inside, so the letter goes within the verb
the letters end up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: first letter of inexpensive
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bit of cheap cushioning unexpectedly halts an eye problem.
explanation.walkthrough: Ptosis is the medical term for a drooping upper eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptosis is the medical name for drooping of the upper eyelid, a condition of that part of the eye.

clue.text: Stay with American writer in South Dakota

indicators.note: the pieces sit inside the state abbreviation

blocks.note: SD is the postal abbreviation for South Dakota
US for American
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An American author is staying put in South Dakota.
explanation.walkthrough: S(US PEN)D.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay a sentence or a proceeding is to suspend it, halting it temporarily.

clue.text: Pull over into a position behind according to established practice

indicators.note: turning a word over reverses it
the reversed word goes into the position word

blocks.note: to lug is to pull or drag
the rear is the position at the back

explanation.surface: A driver is told to pull over behind, as standard procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull over' looks like a police instruction; 'over' reverses LUG to GUL, placed in RE(GUL)AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Regular means conforming to the usual rules or customary procedure.

clue.text: Managed to meet months after party by chance

indicators.note: the months letter follows the party piece in the answer

blocks.note: ran a business means managed it
a do is a party
M is an abbreviation for months

explanation.surface: Two people happened to meet months after a party by luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Random means happening without plan or pattern, as if by accident.

clue.text: Go back on rickety crate carrying rebel leader to Thailand

indicators.note: a word's leader is its first letter
the crate holds the letter inside it
something rickety is shaky and falling apart, so its letters fall out of order
to means added on to the end

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of rebel
T is the international vehicle code for Thailand

explanation.surface: A broken-down crate holding a rebel chief is sent back to Thailand.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a promise or statement is to withdraw it, to renege or go back on it.

clue.text: Help to accommodate retired motorists with tick for example

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so the motorists' initials run backwards
the help word accommodates, holding inside, the other piece

blocks.note: aid is help
the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Support given to elderly drivers, ticking off a checklist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' looks like a mark of approval; it is the bloodsucking mite. A(CAR)ID.
explanation.definitionFit: An acarid is any mite or tick, so a tick is one example of the group.

clue.text: About to find Juliet's suitor against rich clothing and ornaments generally

blocks.note: ca is the abbreviation for circa, about
Count Paris, Juliet's intended husband in Romeo and Juliet
on as in leaning on, set against

explanation.surface: Juliet's wealthy suitor is up against fine robes and finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juliet's suitor' tempts with Romeo; it is the other one, Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: Caparison is ornamental covering for a horse, and more broadly any rich clothing or adornment.

clue.text: A feature of sonnets by Frost say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken and heard

blocks.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A trait of the sonnets written by the poet Robert Frost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet Robert Frost; it is the icy coating, rime.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonnets follow a set scheme of matching line-endings, so this is one of their defining features.

clue.text: Opening line in popular film

indicators.note: the line letter goes inside the other pieces

blocks.note: in means fashionable, popular
E.T., Spielberg's film
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: The first line of a well-loved movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening line' looks like a single phrase; 'Opening' is the definition. IN + L + ET.
explanation.definitionFit: An inlet is a narrow gap or entrance, as in a bay or an air vent, hence an opening.

clue.text: Learning about Italy's principal river

indicators.note: principal means chief or first, so only the first letter is kept
the learning word goes about, around, the other piece

blocks.note: lore is learning or knowledge
first letter of Italy

explanation.surface: Studying the chief river of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italy's principal river' suggests the Po; the answer is a French river. L(I)ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, flowing to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Having ample space for my little bounder at first

indicators.note: at first puts the bounder piece at the front

blocks.note: a roo is a kangaroo, a bounding animal, and Roo is the little kangaroo in Winnie-the-Pooh
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spacious place for my small jumping pet.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means spacious, with plenty of room inside.

clue.text: Highly specialised publications in German removed from various categories

indicators.note: the German letter is taken out of the categories word
various means varied, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for German
taken as written

explanation.surface: Niche German books are excluded from several classifications.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure items, especially books, meant for or understood by only a select few.

clue.text: Penniless pickpockets are inclined to exaggerate

indicators.note: penniless means without a penny, so the penny abbreviation is removed

blocks.note: dips is slang for pickpockets
to tend to do something is to be inclined to

explanation.surface: Broke thieves are prone to overstating things.
explanation.walkthrough: P stands for penny, so DIPS loses P.
explanation.definitionFit: To distend is to swell out or enlarge, so making something bigger than it was, as exaggerating does.

clue.text: Where cricket fans may be seen to demonstrate

definitions.text: Where cricket fans may be seen

blocks.clueFragment: Where cricket fans may be seen
blocks.note: first meaning, split as two words: at a Test, an international cricket match
second meaning: to give proof or evidence of

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words for the first reading: a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness to or prove something, giving evidence that it is true.
